analysis:
The change is confined to a test file, provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Inference/Engine/EngineV2KVBackendGateTests.swift. The visible hunks are around head lines 713-754. They change a lockstep assertion on the paged pool's maxPrefillChunk versus the scheduler's prefillChunkSize and soloPrefillStripeTokens. A new test, widePrefillChunkKeepsPagedPoolGeometry, is added; its patch excerpt is truncated, so its full body is not visible. The updated assertions expect Gemma 4's wide plain chunk (EngineV2Factory.widePrefillChunkTokens) to replace the default solo-prefill stripe (soloPrefillStripeTokens == nil) while the pool geometry stays at defaultSoloPrefillStripeTokens.

No production source is changed in the supplied evidence, so no trust boundary, authorization, attestation, encryption or cache-storage behavior changes. T-041 (prefix cache, SSD tier) is the only provided definition. The tests touch SSDPrefixCache construction with ephemeral keys and temporary roots, but they are unchanged and use isolated temp directories with an in-memory KEK. They do not affect the at-rest posture, TTL, HMAC naming or scope binding.

The security-relevant property is that the paged pool size covers the maximum prefill chunk the engine can schedule. The code comment says PagedSequenceKV preconditions on this and a violation is a process kill (an availability concern). The test strengthens that guard by pinning the pool against the scheduler config. The underlying production change (widePrefillChunkTokens replacing the stripe, and whether the pool is sized as max(chunk, stripe)) is not in the supplied units. A later pass should check that the production pool sizing covers widePrefillChunkTokens when the stripe is nil. The new test's assertion paged.pool.config.maxPrefillChunk == defaultSoloPrefillStripeTokens implies the pool is not resized to the wide chunk. If widePrefillChunkTokens exceeds that value, the lockstep precondition could trip. The visible assertion compares the pool to max(prefillChunkSize, stripe), and the next line pins the pool to the stripe default, so these are consistent only if widePrefillChunkTokens <= defaultSoloPrefillStripeTokens. This could not be verified here, so I flag it as a question and not a finding.
